knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Solids are removed by hand before any water is used, so a hose does not push debris into drains and under equipment.
Hot water and steam can cook protein onto equipment, so a cool or lukewarm rinse is used instead. The other options are not the reason.
A drain holding food debris can produce odour and harbour microorganisms and pests, so it is cleared during each wet clean.

practicalCriteria: Observer confirms that dry removal of all visible solids is complete before the first drop of water is applied (pass: no water used before debris is removed).
Observer confirms that water is kept off motors, panels and dry stores for the whole clean (pass: no contact recorded).
Learner clears and flushes a drain and shows that water flows freely (pass: drain checked and recorded).
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Observer checklist for the dry-then-wet sequence
Before and after photos of the drain, taken by the observer or with consent
Completed zone record for the practical task
stopWorkCriteria: Water is about to be directed at electrical equipment or a motor.
Steam or hot water is being used for a task without training or site approval.
A drain blockage or back-flow appears that cannot be cleared safely.
Wet floors cannot be managed to prevent slips.
